| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="nc">Box</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">&#95;fieldProbeAutoController</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">ShaderFieldAutoController</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | The per-frame controller installed by `Box.fieldProbeAutoControl`, or `null`. Kept on the box so a re-run can stop the previous one before installing its replacement — which is exactly what `fieldProbeAutoControl` does, and why re-running a box does not leave two controllers fighting over the same push constants. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="nc">Box</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">&#95;fieldStatsBinding</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">ShaderFieldStatsBinding</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | How this box is joined to a `ShaderFieldStats` block: the stats object plus whether this box is its *producer* (it owns the buffers and its GLSL records into them) or merely a consumer. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="nc">Once</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">vertex</span> <span class="k">by</span> <span class="nc">Onceing</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | `once.vertex { …GLSL… }` fills the box's `Box.vertex` property from code, the first time only. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="nc">Once</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">fragment</span> <span class="k">by</span> <span class="nc">Onceing</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | `once.fragment { …GLSL… }` fills `Box.fragment` once from code. Same fragment-ordering trap as `Once.vertex`: seed it in a fragment *before* the one that expands `moduleHere`. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="nc">Once</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">vertex&#95;fragment</span> <span class="k">by</span> <span class="nc">Onceing</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | `once.vertex_fragment { …Slang… }` fills `Box.vertex_fragment` once — the shared-Slang route, which overrides whatever `once.vertex`/`once.fragment` put in place. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="nc">Once</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">compute</span> <span class="k">by</span> <span class="nc">Onceing</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | `once.compute { …GLSL… }` fills `Box.compute` once, ahead of the `computeModuleHere` fragment. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="nc">Once</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">task</span> <span class="k">by</span> <span class="nc">Onceing</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | `once.task { …GLSL… }` fills `Box.task` once, ahead of the `meshModuleHere` fragment. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="nc">Once</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">mesh</span> <span class="k">by</span> <span class="nc">Onceing</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | `once.mesh { …GLSL… }` fills `Box.mesh` once, ahead of the `meshModuleHere` fragment. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="nc">Once</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">raygen</span> <span class="k">by</span> <span class="nc">Onceing</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | `once.raygen { …GLSL… }` fills `Box.raygen` once, ahead of the `rayTracingModuleHere` fragment. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="nc">Once</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">miss</span> <span class="k">by</span> <span class="nc">Onceing</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | `once.miss { …GLSL… }` fills `Box.miss` once; leave it unset to build a pipeline with no miss stage at all. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="nc">Once</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">closesthit</span> <span class="k">by</span> <span class="nc">Onceing</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | `once.closesthit { …GLSL… }` fills `Box.closesthit` once. Optional stage. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="nc">Once</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">anyhit</span> <span class="k">by</span> <span class="nc">Onceing</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | `once.anyhit { …GLSL… }` fills `Box.anyhit` once. Optional stage. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="nc">Once</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">intersection</span> <span class="k">by</span> <span class="nc">Onceing</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | `once.intersection { …GLSL… }` fills `Box.intersection` once. Optional stage. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="nc">Once</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">callable</span> <span class="k">by</span> <span class="nc">Onceing</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | `once.callable { …GLSL… }` fills `Box.callable` once. Optional stage. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="nc">Box</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">shaderTemplate</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">MutableMap</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="nc">Any</span><span class="p">&gt;</span></code> | The named values this box's `{{ slot }}` template expressions resolve against — the mechanism behind the shadertoy preamble and any GLSL boilerplate you would rather write once. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="nc">Box</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">stackAutoShaderSources</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">MutableMap</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">&gt;</span></code> | StackSL source, by `stack.auto` slot name, for every `{{ stack.auto.foo }}` this box's shaders declare. Concurrent, because the compile/reload path reads it off the main thread. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">defaultVertexShader</span></code> | The vertex shader a box gets if `moduleHere` expands and the box has no vertex source of its own: one `vec3 pos` input transformed by a `push_constant` block of two `mat4`s, `p` and `m`. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">defaultFragmentShader</span></code> | The fragment shader a box gets if `moduleHere` expands with no fragment source of its own: a flat warm orange, chosen so "it drew *something*" is unmistakable. Declares no uniforms, so it generates no accessors. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">shadertoyVertexShader</span></code> | The vertex shader `shadertoyHere` seeds: no inputs at all, just a full-screen triangle synthesised from `gl_VertexIndex`. That is why the shadertoy module needs a 3-vertex mesh and no vertex buffer. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">shadertoyFragmentShader</span></code> | The fragment shader `shadertoyHere` seeds: the `{{ shadertoy.fragmentPreamble }}` slot (which brings in the `iResolution`/`iTime`/`iMouse`/… uniform block and the `#define`s that make them look like shadertoy globals), a `main` that calls `mainImage`, and a placeholder `mainImage` drawing a uv gradient that pulses with `iTime`. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="nc">Box</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">customTextureResolver</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="nc">Box</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">-</span></code> | A hook for deciding yourself what a shader's `sampler2D someName` should be bound to, consulted before Field's own by-name search of the box's properties. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">defaultRaygenShader</span></code> | The ray-generation shader a box gets when `rayTracingModuleHere` expands and the box has no `raygen` source: it writes the launch uv into the ray payload and traces nothing at all. |

### ShaderIncludeRootRequest { #shaders-kt-shaderincluderootrequest }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">ShaderIncludeRootRequest</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">root</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">includePath</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">requestedPath</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">requestingSourcePath</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">?</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">includeType</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">ShaderIncludeType</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">includeDepth</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span><span class="p">)</span></code>

One `#include` that landed inside a registered include root, handed to a [`ShaderIncludeRootResolver`](graphics.md#shaders-kt-shaderincluderootresolver) to turn into text.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">root</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | The registered root name that matched — the first path segment of a `root/…` include, or, for a relative include, the root the *including* file itself came from. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">includePath</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | The path within `root`, normalised: separators unified to `/`, `.` and empty segments dropped, `..` resolved (and rejected if it would escape the root), no leading slash. This is the key a resolver should look up. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">requestedPath</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | Exactly what the `#include` said, root prefix and all. Useful in diagnostics; do not resolve against it. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">requestingSourcePath</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | The resolved path of the file doing the including (a previous resolution's `resolvedPath`, or a `field/<box>-<id>/<property>.glsl` name for box source), or `null` when shaderc did not supply one. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">includeType</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">ShaderIncludeType</span></code> | `RELATIVE` for `#include "…"`, `STANDARD` for `#include <…>`. Only `RELATIVE` includes are resolved relative to `requestingSourcePath`'s directory. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">includeDepth</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span></code> | How deep this include is nested, straight from shaderc. Informational — nothing in Field enforces a limit on it. |

### ShaderIncludeRootResolver { #shaders-kt-shaderincluderootresolver }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="k">interface</span> <span class="nc">ShaderIncludeRootResolver</span></code>

Turns an include inside one registered root into source text. Register one under a name with `registerShaderIncludeRoot` and every `#include "thatName/whatever.glsl"` in every box's shaders goes through it.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">resolve</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">request</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">ShaderIncludeRootRequest</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">ShaderIncludeResolution</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | Resolve one include, or return `null` if this root does not have it (which the caller turns into a hard error). |

### ShaderRemoteIncludeCacheOptions { #shaders-kt-shaderremoteincludecacheoptions }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">ShaderRemoteIncludeCacheOptions</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">cacheDirectory</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Path</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">connectTimeoutMillis</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">5</span><span class="n">&#95;000</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">readTimeoutMillis</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">5</span><span class="n">&#95;000</span><span class="p">)</span></code>

Where a URL-backed include root keeps its on-disk copies, and how patient it is with the network.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">cacheDirectory</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Path</span></code> | Directory the fetched includes are mirrored into, one file per include path. Created on demand. Resolved to an absolute, normalised path, and includes that would escape it are rejected — a remote server cannot talk you into writing outside this directory. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">connectTimeoutMillis</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | `HttpURLConnection` connect timeout, in milliseconds. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">readTimeoutMillis</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | `HttpURLConnection` read timeout, in milliseconds. Both timeouts are felt by whichever thread is compiling — the main runloop, on the reload path — so the defaults are deliberately short. |

### ShaderProbeAutoControlConfig { #shaders-kt-shaderprobeautocontrolconfig }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">ShaderProbeAutoControlConfig</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">minSamples</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">128</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">clipLower</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="o">?</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.0</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">clipUpper</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="o">?</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">1.0</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">clipEpsilon</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">1.0e</span><span class="p">-</span><span class="mi">6</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">useNominalParams</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">false</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">displayChannel</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">?</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s">&quot;auto&quot;</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">closeDisplayOnStop</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">false</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">clearDisplayOnStop</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">false</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">runloopKeySuffix</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s">&quot;shaderFieldAuto&quot;</span><span class="p">)</span></code>

How `Box.fieldProbeAutoControl` turns probe read-backs into controller updates: when a batch is big enough to act on, what counts as clipped, and where the diagnostics card goes.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">minSamples</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | Minimum samples in a read-back before the controller is allowed to learn from it. A snapshot with fewer is skipped entirely — `tick()` returns `null` and nothing is applied. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">clipLower</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | Values at or below this (within `clipEpsilon`) count as clipped low and are reported to the controller as a clip rate; `null` means "nothing clips at the bottom". |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">clipUpper</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | Values at or above this (within `clipEpsilon`) count as clipped high; `null` means nothing clips at the top. With both bounds `null` the reported clip rate is a flat `0.0`. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">clipEpsilon</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span></code> | Tolerance for the two clip comparisons — floating-point slop, not a percentage. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">useNominalParams</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code> | `true` applies the controller's *nominal* parameters, `false` (the default) its *applied* ones, which carry the small dither the controller needs to identify the system. Turn it on once identification has settled and the dither is visible in the output. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">displayChannel</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | Box output channel for the HTML diagnostics table (nominal vs applied parameters, objective, confidence, clip rate, p10/p50/p90). `null` disables the display entirely, which is what a headless test wants. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">closeDisplayOnStop</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code> | Whether `stop()` closes the display channel by default. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">clearDisplayOnStop</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code> | Whether `stop()` clears the display channel's contents by default. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">runloopKeySuffix</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | Prefix of the runloop hook key, which is `"$runloopKeySuffix:${box.id}"`. Two controllers on one box need two different values here or the second silently displaces the first. |

### ShaderFieldAutoController { #shaders-kt-shaderfieldautocontroller }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">ShaderFieldAutoController</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">box</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Box</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">probe</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">ShaderFieldProbe</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">controller</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">AdaptiveDistributionController</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">config</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">ShaderProbeAutoControlConfig</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">private</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">apply</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="n">params</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">DoubleArray</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">output</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">ControlOutput</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">batch</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FieldProbeScalarBatch</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="o">-&gt;</span> <span class="nc">Unit</span><span class="p">)</span></code>

The running loop that closes a shader's feedback circuit: read the probe, push the samples into an adaptive controller, hand the new parameters to your `apply` lambda, and draw the diagnostics.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">box</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Box</span></code> | The box this controller belongs to: the source of the display channel and the identity in the runloop hook key. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">probe</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">ShaderFieldProbe</span></code> | The probe being read. `Box.fieldProbeAutoControl` has already put it into continuous-read mode, so it delivers a snapshot every frame rather than at the display rate. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">controller</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">AdaptiveDistributionController</span></code> | The adaptive controller doing the actual learning; its `parameterNames` label the diagnostics table and its `pushSamples` is what turns a batch into parameters. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">config</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">ShaderProbeAutoControlConfig</span></code> | The thresholds, clip bounds and display settings this controller was built with. Read on every tick, but the object is immutable — copy it and rebuild to change your mind. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">tickCount</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | How many ticks have actually done work. Ticks that found no new snapshot, or too few samples, do not count — so a `tickCount` stuck at zero means the probe is not delivering, not that the hook is missing. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">lastBatch</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FieldProbeScalarBatch</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | The last probe batch the controller learned from, or `null` before the first useful tick. Carries both the raw snapshot and the clip rate computed from `config`. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">lastOutput</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">ControlOutput</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | The last controller output — nominal and applied parameters plus diagnostics — or `null` before the first useful tick. The same object the `apply` lambda was handed. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">tick</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">ControlOutput</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | Do one control step, returning the controller's output, or `null` if there was nothing to do. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">install</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">runloop</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Runloop</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">Runloop</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">runLoop</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">ShaderFieldAutoController</span></code> | Install a `preRun` hook that calls `tick` once per frame, and return `this` for chaining. Idempotent — a second call while already installed does nothing. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">stop</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">runloop</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Runloop</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">Runloop</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">runLoop</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">closeDisplay</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">config</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">closeDisplayOnStop</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">clearDisplay</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">config</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">clearDisplayOnStop</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">ShaderFieldAutoController</span></code> | Remove the runloop hook, optionally tidy the display channel, and forget this controller on the box. Returns `this`, and can be re-`install`ed afterwards. |

## spatial_field.kt { #spatial-field-kt }

The bridges out of Field's plane-geometry results and into the things Field already draws.

Every partitioner in `graph_connectivity.kt`, `dirichlet.kt`, `contours.kt` and `clustering.kt`
answers with *structure* — cell vertex rings, circular arcs, triangle index triples, cluster
labels — and none of them answers with geometry. This file is the missing hop: one `toFLines` per
result type, so a Voronoi diagram, an Apollonius cell, a Delaunay triangulation or a k-medoids
partition lands in the same drawing, animation and export machinery as anything drawn by hand.
It is the plane counterpart of `mesh_field.kt`, which does the same job for `TriMesh`.

Two layers:

 1. **Structure → `FLine`.** `PointGraph.toFLine`, `delaunayTrianglesToFLine`,
    `VoronoiDiagram.toFLines`, `CircularDirichlet.Diagram.toFLines`,
    `CircularDirichlet.CellBoundary.toFLines`, `ClusterLayer.toFLines` and
    `pointCloudFLine`. Each returns styled, drawable lines and nothing else — no `Box`, no
    output, so they are usable from a test or a renderer as readily as from a box.
 2. **`FLine` → a captioned figure.** `Box.showPlane` and `Box.showPlaneGrid` rasterise lines to
    inline SVG with `drawToSVG` and push a titled card — live and pannable for one figure, frozen
    for a grid of them — to a box output channel: the fastest way to see a whole pipeline at once,
    and the 2D twin of `Box.showMeshGrid`. `planeFigureHtml` is the markup on its own.

The figure helpers are AWT-free (Skia's SVG canvas, same as `Box.lines`), so they work headless,
including inside the docs build.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/stdlib/spatial_field.kt`

**Used in:** [Points into structure — Voronoi, Apollonius, contours and clusters](../spatial_geometry_examples.md), [Which of these signals actually depend on each other?](../statistics_examples.md)

## stacksl.kt { #stacksl-kt }

Host-side entry points for StackSL: compiling the stack language to GLSL, and evaluating it on
the GPU sample by sample. The language, its compiler and its diagnostics live in
`afield.stacksl`; this file is the Kotlin surface a box calls.

`stackSL` holds a box's StackSL source, falling back to a parent box's. `compileStackSL`,
`stackSLToGlsl` and the standalone `slGlsl` are pure compilation and need no device. `slEval` and
`slSweep` actually run the compiled function: they wrap it in a small compute shader and dispatch
it through a `Renderer` that defaults to `fromContext()`, so they need a live graphics context.
Neither binds any texture sampler, so a source that needs one is rejected.

`slSweep` returns a [`StackSLSweep`](graphics.md#stacksl-kt-stackslsweep), which implements `ToHTML` and draws itself as an inline SVG
plot of the four output channels with per-channel min/median/max; `StackSLSweep.h` is that HTML.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/stdlib/stacksl.kt`

**Used in:** [StackSL cheatsheet](../stacksl_cheatsheet.md), [StackSL examples](../stacksl_examples.md)

### Top-level functions { #stacksl-kt-functions }

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nc">Box</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">stackSLPrefix</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | A GLSL-safe identifier prefix unique to this box — `stacksl_` plus the first 12 characters of the box id with `-` turned into `_` (`stacksl_box` for a box with a blank id). |

## typography.kt { #typography-kt }

Text as geometry: a string becomes contours, and from there everything Field already does to
geometry applies to letters.

Field can draw, mesh, filter, cluster, contour and evolve geometry, and before this file it could
not turn *a string* into any of it. Every `java.awt.Font` in the tree paints a label into a
raster — `MeshGallery`, `ImagingGallery`, `montage`'s 5x7 bitmap font — and none of them produces a
value you can extrude, march, sample or animate. This file and its bridge companion
`typography_field.kt` are that missing layer, and they need no new dependency:
`Font.createGlyphVector(...).getOutline()` hands back real quadratic/cubic glyph outlines, and it
works headless.

### The three values

 - [`Typeface`](graphics.md#typography-kt-typeface) — a font at a size, from a logical/system name (`typeface`) or a `.ttf`/`.otf` on
   disk (`typefaceFromFile`). Carries the vertical metrics (ascent, descent, leading) a layout
   needs.
 - [`Glyph`](graphics.md#typography-kt-glyph) — one glyph's outline, cached per typeface and glyph code, in its own frame with its
   origin on its own baseline. Both representations live side by side: `Glyph.contours` are
   flattened, nesting-classified, winding-normalised polygons for geometry work, and
   `Glyph.outline` is the same rings as an `FLine` of *real cubics* for drawing.
 - [`TextLayout`](graphics.md#typography-kt-textlayout) — glyphs placed on baselines by AWT's own advances and kerning, plus tracking,
   multi-line and alignment. Every glyph in it is a [`PlacedGlyph`](graphics.md#typography-kt-placedglyph) carrying **mutable transform
   handles** (offset, rotation, scale, pivot). Those handles are the API, not an afterthought:
   they are what makes kinetic typography a two-line box body, and `TextLayout.onCurve` is
   nothing but a routine that sets them from an `FLine`'s arc length.

### Text space

Glyph and layout coordinates are **x right, y down**, origin at the first baseline, units = the
typeface's size in points. That is AWT's own glyph frame and it is also the frame Field's 2D
outputs use (`Rect`'s y grows downwards), so text handed straight to `Box.lines` or
`Box.showText` reads the right way up with no transform. The 3D bridges in `typography_field.kt`
flip y at their own boundary, because a mesh wants y up.

### The winding convention

A glyph's counter — the hole in `o`, `e`, `a`, `B` — is only a hole if something says so, and
"whatever the font shipped" is not good enough: `isoContourFLines` in `contours.kt` leaves winding
arbitrary and every consumer downstream has to cope. So this file *decides*:

> For a ring `p0..pn`, signed area is `½Σ(xᵢyᵢ₊₁ − xᵢ₊₁yᵢ)` in text space. **Outer contours are
> positive; holes are negative.** A ring's `GlyphContour.depth` — how many other rings of the same
> glyph contain it — is authoritative: even depth is an outer contour, odd depth is a hole. A ring
> whose area sign disagrees with its depth is *reversed* on the way out.

Both representations obey it, so `contours.filter { it.isHole }` and the subpaths of
`Glyph.outline` agree, and `TypographyTest` asserts it on glyphs whose answer is known by eye
(`o` has one hole, `l` has none, `%` has two). Depth comes from point-in-polygon containment and
the sign comes from the area formula, so the assertion compares two independent computations
rather than restating one of them.

### AWT and the main run loop

`imaging_field.kt:417` explains why `montage` captions with a bitmap table instead of
`Graphics2D.drawString`: on macOS, touching the AWT font manager pulls in AppKit, which competes
with GLFW for the main run loop, and `Server.main` deliberately never initialises the toolkit. This
family cannot avoid the font manager — it *is* the font manager — so it contains the hazard in one
place, `Typefaces.warm`, whose KDoc carries the measured stack trace and the conclusion:

> **A JVM that wants glyph outlines and passes `-XstartOnFirstThread` must also pass
> `-Djava.awt.headless=true`.** Otherwise `CFontManager.loadFonts` dispatches to the process's first
> thread and waits forever for a run loop nobody is pumping.

`Typefaces.warm` detects that in four seconds and throws with that sentence in it, rather than
hanging the editor. Every jvm-main gallery in the tree already sets the property in the first line
of `main`, `jvmTest` does not need it (Gradle's test JVM has no `-XstartOnFirstThread`), and an
interactive Field window pumps its run loop through `glfwPollEvents` and so is expected to be
fine — expected, not tested; see `Typefaces.warm`. Everything after that one touch is pure
computation over cached outlines.

## typography_field.kt { #typography-field-kt }

The bridges out of a [`TextLayout`](graphics.md#typography-kt-textlayout) and into the four families Field already has.

`typography.kt` answers with *structure* — rings, depths, advances, handles — and structure is not
yet a drawing, a mesh, an image or a point cloud. This file is the missing hop, and it is the
reason the typography family is worth having at all: once a string is contours, letters get to be
inputs to machinery that never knew about text.

It is the typographic counterpart of `spatial_field.kt` (plane geometry → `FLine`) and
`mesh_field.kt` (`TriMesh` → `FLine`), and it is written to the same rule: every function here
returns a *value* — no `Box`, no output — except the two figure helpers at the bottom, which are
`drawToSVG` and so work headless, in a test and in the docs build.

Five bridges:

 1. **→ `FLine`** (`TextLayout.toFLines`, `TextLayout.toFLine`, `Glyph.toFLine`). One line per
    glyph, so a per-glyph handle actually moves something, with the font's real cubics intact.
    Filling works because of `typography.kt`'s winding convention and nothing else: Skia and
    Java2D both fill non-zero, so a counter is a hole precisely because its ring runs the other
    way. `TextLayout.toFLines` takes `honourHoles = false` to show you the blob you get without a
    convention, which is the control arm the docs figure uses.
 2. **→ [`TriMesh`](graphics.md#mesh-kt-trimesh)** (`TextLayout.toMesh`). Hole-aware extrusion: `extrudeMesh` in
    `mesh_generate.kt:619` and `triangulatePolygon` (`:547`) explicitly cannot do holes, so the
    caps here go through `FloatEarcut` with hole indices and the walls are emitted ring by ring
    from the *same* flattened vertices, which is what makes the result watertight — and makes an
    extruded `o` genus 1 and an extruded `l` genus 0.
 3. **→ an SDF** (`TextLayout.toSdf`). A 2D signed-distance grid, bilinearly sampled and extruded
    in z, so letters compose with `sdfSphere`, `sdfSmoothUnion`, `.twisted()` and everything else
    in `mesh_sdf.kt`, and `marchingCubes` will mesh the result.
 4. **→ [`Img`](imaging.md#imaging-kt-img)** (`rasterizeText`). An analytic even-odd scanline fill of the layout's own rings —
    deliberately *not* `Graphics2D.drawString`, both because AWT text rendering in-process is what
    `imaging_field.kt:417` forbids and because filling our own outlines means a legible PNG is
    evidence about *this* code rather than about AWT's rasteriser.
 5. **→ points** (`TextLayout.samplePoints`, `TextLayout.toPointFLine`). Even-by-arc-length
    samples along the outlines, which is what the alife agents, the clusterers and the
    contourers in `clustering.kt` / `alife_agents.kt` consume.

Frames: bridges 1, 3, 4 and 5 stay in text space (y **down**, origin on the first baseline);
bridge 2 flips y at its boundary, because a mesh wants y up, and re-normalises winding when it
does.

## voronoi.kt { #voronoi-kt }

Practical 3D Voronoi and approximate 3D multiplicatively weighted Voronoi
("CircularDirichlet") for Kotlin + Field linalg.

- `voronoi3d` builds convex polyhedral cells by intersecting pairwise bisector half-spaces. Six
  clip-box planes are added to **every** cell, not only to the unbounded ones, so a cell always
  comes back as a bounded polyhedron; `VoronoiCell3.bounded` is how you tell whether the answer is
  the site's own cell or an artefact of the box. The box is the sites' bounding box grown on every
  side by `clipPadding * scale + 1`, where `scale` is the cloud's own diagonal (floored at 1).
- `CircularDirichlet3d.build` extracts approximate support patches on bisector spheres / planes by
  clipping a sampled surface mesh with the weighted score predicate.

The weighted contourer is renderer-oriented: it prefers stable, wound
boundary loops over exact symbolic patch topology.

### What the unweighted clipper guarantees, and what it does not

Which face each corner belongs to is decided **combinatorially** — a corner records the planes that
produced it, and a face's polygon is exactly the corners recording that plane — rather than by a
distance test against a tolerance. See the `collectCorners` KDoc in [`Voronoi3d`](graphics.md#voronoi-kt-voronoi3d) for why that matters: with a
tolerance scaled off the point cloud, faces near a near-cospherical site cluster claimed corners
that were not on them, and the cells did not close (a T-junction, and a hairline crack in any mesh
built from the faces).

It is still a `Float` clipper and the repair is not total. On the sweep that ratcheted it, **4 of
465 bounded cells** and **12 of 447 clipped cells** still fail the strict closure check — every
edge walked by exactly two faces, in opposite directions. Those counts are pinned with `<=` in
`VoronoiFaceTopologyTest`, so they can improve but cannot regress silently. Cell volumes tile the
clip box to 1e-4 relative and a cubic lattice of sites gives exact unit cubes.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/stdlib/voronoi.kt`

**Used in:** [Points into structure — Voronoi, Apollonius, contours and clusters](../spatial_geometry_examples.md), [Meshes and 3D geometry](../mesh_examples.md)

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">SupportPlane3</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">normal</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Vec3</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">d</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">SupportSurface3</span></code>

The ordinary perpendicular bisector plane, which is what a weighted bisector degenerates to when the two weights are equal (within the build tolerance).

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">normal</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Vec3</span></code> | The plane's normal, not normalized. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">d</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | The offset: the plane is the points `x` with `dot(normal, x) == d`. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">samplePoint</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Vec3</span></code> | The point on the plane closest to the origin. |

### CircularDirichletPatch3 { #voronoi-kt-circulardirichletpatch3 }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">sealed</span> <span class="k">interface</span> <span class="nc">CircularDirichletPatch3</span></code>

One piece of one cell's boundary in the weighted diagram: the part of a bisector surface that is actually on the boundary once every *other* site has had its say.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">siteIndex</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | The cell this patch bounds. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">neighborSite</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | The site on the other side of it. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">support</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">SupportSurface3</span></code> | The unbounded surface this patch was cut out of. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">truncated</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code> | `true` when the clip box cut this patch, so its extent is the window's and not the sites'. |

### SpherePatch3 { #voronoi-kt-spherepatch3 }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">SpherePatch3</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">siteIndex</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">neighborSite</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">support</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">SupportSphere3</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">boundary</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Vec3</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">truncated</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">CircularDirichletPatch3</span></code>

A patch of an Apollonius sphere.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">siteIndex</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | The cell this patch bounds. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">neighborSite</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | The site on the other side of it. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">support</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">SupportSphere3</span></code> | The sphere this patch lies on. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">boundary</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Vec3</span><span class="p">&gt;</span></code> | The patch outline as a wound loop of points on the sphere, or **empty to mean the entire sphere** rather than an empty patch (an empty patch is not emitted at all). |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">truncated</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code> | `true` when the clip box cut this patch, so its extent is the window's and not the sites'. |

### PlanePatch3 { #voronoi-kt-planepatch3 }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">PlanePatch3</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">siteIndex</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">neighborSite</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">support</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">SupportPlane3</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">polygon</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Vec3</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">truncated</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">CircularDirichletPatch3</span></code>

A patch of an ordinary bisector plane, between two equally-weighted sites.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">siteIndex</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | The cell this patch bounds. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">neighborSite</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | The site on the other side of it. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">support</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">SupportPlane3</span></code> | The plane this patch lies on. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">polygon</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Vec3</span><span class="p">&gt;</span></code> | The patch outline as a wound loop of points on the plane. Never empty. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">truncated</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code> | `true` when the clip box cut this patch, so its extent is the window's and not the sites'. |

### CircularDirichletCell3 { #voronoi-kt-circulardirichletcell3 }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">CircularDirichletCell3</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">siteIndex</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">patches</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">CircularDirichletPatch3</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">)</span></code>

One weighted cell, as the collection of boundary patches that fence it in.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">siteIndex</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | Which weighted site this is the cell of. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">patches</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">CircularDirichletPatch3</span><span class="p">&gt;</span></code> | The boundary pieces, sorted by `CircularDirichletPatch3.neighborSite` then by support size. |

### CircularDirichletDiagram3 { #voronoi-kt-circulardirichletdiagram3 }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">CircularDirichletDiagram3</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">cells</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">CircularDirichletCell3</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">clipBounds</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Aabb3</span><span class="p">)</span></code>

| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">cells</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">CircularDirichletCell3</span><span class="p">&gt;</span></code> | One cell per input site, in input order. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">clipBounds</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Aabb3</span></code> | The box the patches were clipped against, built the same way as `VoronoiLattice.clipBounds`. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">operator</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">get</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">siteIndex</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">CircularDirichletCell3</span></code> | The cell of site `siteIndex`. |

| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">build</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">sites</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">WeightedSite3</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">tolerance</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">1e</span><span class="p">-</span><span class="mi">4f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">clipPadding</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">8f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">sphereSubdivisions</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">3</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">planeSteps</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">56</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">CircularDirichletDiagram3</span></code> | Build the weighted diagram of `sites`. |
